executive_summary: The release will enable project managers to access a detailed engagement history for each country before starting new missions, which includes timestamps, record notes, and outcomes. However, key issues related to retention policies and data destruction timelines remain unresolved and require further clarification. Decision-makers will need to address compliance and confidentiality aspects to ensure the information is properly managed and protected.

core_commitments.text: Project managers can view a detailed engagement history for each country.
core_commitments.note: Project managers can now view a detailed engagement history for each country, ensuring they have necessary information for new missions.

core_commitments.text: The engagement history includes timestamps, record notes, and outcomes.
core_commitments.note: The engagement history will include timestamps, record notes, and outcomes, providing comprehensive insights into previous interactions.

in_scope.text: Project managers will have access to a dedicated 'Engagement History' section in the CRM.
in_scope.note: Project managers will have access to a dedicated 'Engagement History' section in the CRM, facilitating ease of use.

in_scope.text: Engagement history means all recorded interactions with government counterparts, including meetings, communications, and notes.
in_scope.note: The definition of engagement history has been clarified to include all recorded interactions, ensuring project managers have complete information.

in_scope.text: The system will display engagement history for all countries with which there is a past record in the CRM.
in_scope.note: The system will display engagement history for all countries with past records, allowing project managers to access necessary data.

in_scope.text: Users can filter the engagement history by date range and type of interaction.
in_scope.note: Users can filter the engagement history by date range and type of interaction, enabling targeted searches for relevant information.

in_scope.text: Upon a project manager's transition out of their role, their access to sensitive engagement records will be revoked immediately by the system administrator responsible for managing user access, in compliance with the organization's security policy.
in_scope.note: Access to sensitive records will be revoked immediately when a project manager transitions out of their role, ensuring compliance with security policies.

in_scope.text: The system will maintain an audit trail of all changes made to engagement history records, documenting the user who made the change, the timestamp of the modification, and the specifics of what was changed. This audit trail will undergo quarterly reviews by designated compliance officers to ensure adherence to data governance standards.
in_scope.note: An audit trail of changes to engagement history will be maintained, enhancing accountability and compliance with governance standards.

in_scope.text: The system will implement a data validation process to ensure the accuracy and freshness of engagement history records, conducted by designated personnel who have a minimum of 3 years of experience in data quality management and governance, with relevant certifications in data protection and management best practices. This validation process will occur bi-annually.
in_scope.note: A bi-annual data validation process will be implemented to maintain accuracy, specifying required qualifications for personnel involved.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not implement any changes to user roles or security clearances outside of current definitions.
out_of_scope.note: The release will not implement changes to user roles or security clearances outside current definitions to maintain control.

out_of_scope.text: The release will not provide access to engagement records of countries that are not involved in any active missions.
out_of_scope.note: This release will not provide access to records from non-active missions, focusing only on relevant historical data.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include any real-time updates from ongoing engagements; it will only display historical data.
out_of_scope.note: Real-time updates from ongoing engagements are out of scope, as this feature will only display historical data.

assumptions.text: Project managers are users of the CRM with the necessary permissions to access engagement histories.
assumptions.note: It is assumed project managers have the necessary permissions to access engagement histories, ensuring smooth functionality.

assumptions.text: Engagement records are currently stored in a structured way that allows for filtering and retrieval.
assumptions.note: Assumed structured storage of engagement records will facilitate filtering and retrieval, critical for project managers.

assumptions.text: There are existing records of past engagements with each country that can be extracted for display.
assumptions.note: Expecting existing records of past engagements is key for displaying data effectively in the engagement history section.

assumptions.text: The organization has policies in place to uphold data protection and privacy regarding sensitive contacts.
assumptions.note: The organization's data protection and privacy policies are assumed to be in place to protect sensitive contacts.

definitions.text: 'Engagement history' means the chronological record of all interactions, communications, and engagements with a government contact or agency, including meeting dates, notes, and outcomes. Sensitive records within this engagement history will be flagged using classification labels clearly visible in the interface, with corresponding access requirements outlined next to each record. Unauthorized access attempts will trigger notifications to security personnel.
definitions.note: The definition of engagement history now clearly states what types of records are included and how sensitive data will be flagged.

success_criteria.text: At least 80% of project managers report they can easily access and utilize the engagement history feature based on a post-deployment survey.
success_criteria.note: Success criteria set to ensure at least 80% satisfaction from project managers regarding the accessibility of the new feature.
